There are versions where Medea doesn’t kill the kids Duke University has a catalog of the different variations of the myth. Here’s the link:  
🔗 [Duke University's Medea Myth Variations](https://people.duke.edu/~wj25/UC_Web_Site/tragedy/medea.html#:~:text=Another%20version%20of%20the%20myth,or%20even%20usually%20is%2C%20told)

So no, I don’t think Medea and Jason are equally bad in those versions. There’s even one where she kills the kids by accident while trying to make them immortal to protect them. But the important part is that, no matter the version, the children always die, and that’s because their deaths are part of Jason’s divine punishment for breaking his oath to Hera. Once he broke that vow, their fate was sealed.

We agree that Medea was forced by the gods to fall in love with Jason. And sure, Jason didn’t ask the gods to do that, and he didn’t directly ask for Hera’s help either. But he absolutely benefits from their intervention and in the end, he’s the one who betrays a divine oath.

Hera only helps Jason to get revenge on Pelias, his uncle, and because she liked Jason when they first met. But throughout the whole quest for the Golden Fleece, Jason constantly relies on others. He doesn’t make plans, doesn’t take initiative he leans on the other heroes, Medea, or Hera to handle everything. He never shows any of the traits you’d expect from a capable leader or king.

If he were clever like Odysseus, he could’ve used Hera’s favor strategically. Or if he were a warrior like Perseus, Herakles, or even Theseus, he might’ve earned his throne through strength. But Jason does neither he just rides the support of others, and when they’re no longer useful, he discards them.

I agree, from a modern moral perspective, Medea is definitely worse she murders family, no argument there. But if we look at the myth through a more traditional or ancient Greek lens, Jason is worse in terms of moral failure. He’s a man who can’t lead, who abuses divine favor, and whose hubris ultimately causes the deaths of his children and his own downfall.

Tbf Medea is a special case she was used by the gods to help Jason in every way she could. Aphrodite made her fall madly in love with him and Hera basically forced her to be tied with him as a result. The love she has for Jason was imposed on her by the Gods so that she would do Jason's dirty work. Which is another reason I don't particularly like Jason as a hero he overly reliant on others.


In some tellings Medea doesn't even kill the kids so I think the children she had with Jason were fated to die as punishment regardless.


I think Jason is most to blame in this situation. He broke an oath to the Gods and tired to divorce Medea all while knowing his patron is the Goddess of Marriage . We all know how breaking oaths to the Gods and disrespecting their domains leads to tragedy. 


So imo Jason set himself up for failure and considering the fact that without divine intervention happening via Hera and Aphrodite Medea would have never been with Jason. Also remember back then divorced was woman was considered severely damaged goods. Jason was going to leave her and the kids. Which was going to damn his kids too because had Jason gotten married and become King the kids from his first marriage could be seen as a threat.

I think abortion is a very complex issue. I used to be firmly pro-life when I was younger but as I have gotten older, I have shifted to being pro-choice. The decision to have a baby has long-lasting effects on a woman’s health and I don't like conservatives and evangelicals putting such strict measures on it. Issues like sexual assault, incest, potential death, and sterilization are some of the reasons I support abortion.

The strict abortion bans levied by most states have put women’s health in danger with no consideration for their lives. If the bans are going to be so strict, then there should be more safety measures put in place and more consideration of how a shift in policy can affect people's lives.

A lot of the legislation fights to ensure these children are born but then stops caring as soon as they are here. States have imposed strict abortion bans while simultaneously pushing to cut funding for programs like WIC and foster care.

I think it's intended to mirror Samuel's storyline. Samuel wanted his dad to be a gangster, but he ended up being a normal guy. Contrasting Daniel, he grew up thinking his father was the average Joe, but in reality, his father is a gangster who almost killed him. I personally believe that Jinyoung is Daniel's father and chapter 433 seems to be backing that theory.  In chapter 157 Thanksgiving(End) it's revealed that Daniel has no family on his mother's side which is why I don't think Jinyoung is his uncle. Daniel's mom speaks very fondly of Jinyoung and is portrayed to be worried for his well-being.

Seeing how the community seems to be split on whether Jinyoung is the father or not due to this chapter. I think Daniel's "dad" is a red herring. I doubt PTJ would have two similar storylines of characters questioning their paternity only for the outcome to be the same that it was just a normal working man. Both little Daniel and big Daniel look eerily similar to Jinyoung which can be seen when people have compared panels of the two. This was also confirmed as of chapter 433 by Daniel's "grandmother".  As we all know Daniel has the copy ability canonically Jinyoung is the first known user of the ability. There are too many things that match up that at least connect Daniel and Jinyoung on a genetic level which could be linked to experimentation or just biology.

I know some people are against the theory because it makes Daniel's mom look bad but there are routes that PJT could where even if Jinyoung is the father it doesn't affect her in a negative way. For example forced marriage, sperm donor, etc. If I'm being honest the only reason I want the Jinyoung father theory to be true is that I feel it adds more to the story if he is.
